utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, The Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic, et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. All the accused are here. From the Defence teams, I only notice the absence of Mr. Haynes. Prosecution, it's Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Thayer and Mr. Vanderpuye. All right. Is there a reason why the witness is not in the courtroom as yet? Are there preliminaries? Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, everyone. We did want to raise one preliminary with the Trial Chamber. Things have -- got a little interesting yesterday and since, and I'm going to sort of work with my colleagues here. I'm sure if I'm entering into areas that they're not comfortable with me raising with the Trial Chamber, they'll let me know. But out of an abundance of caution, given the Court's decision to call back the prior witness, given some further investigation that was conducted in light of what that witness testified to, that investigation also being conducted after the court session yesterday, we developed some additional evidence. So one of the things we want to do is get an idea from the Trial Chamber just generally what the procedure will be and also to advise the Trial Chamber what -- frankly how I intend to proceed with the cross-examination of the witness upon some of this new information just so that there's no mystery. I've CC'd the Trial Chamber's legal officers last night with respect to the new investigation which was conducted with respect to this issue. I do not know whether this new issue is something that is of interest to the Trial Chamber with respect to recalling the witness. That is why I went ahead and forwarded it to the legal officers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, sorry to interrupt you like this, which is not exactly our style, but if -- there seems to be a mysterious shroud before you started your intervention. It has certainly become much more obscure and cloudy. We don't know what you are talking about. We have not had any communication from our senior legal officer. The only information, additional information that we have is that there is an addition to your list of exhibits. That is the only thing that we know, something that has to do with the Hotel Fontana, but that's about it. Otherwise, we have no further information. We don't even know -- although I have had my usual morning meeting with our senior legal officer, he hasn't even informed me that he received anything from you. So what I suggest, I don't know, because there is another tale to it. It seems, if I'm reading you well, that you would like some time to have a word with your counterpart, with Mr. Ostojic, if I understood you well.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I frankly don't think that's necessary. I mean, I'll be happy to hear from my friend. I think the Prosecution's position is pretty clear from the supplemental information report that we disclosed last night. But I'm happy, as I said, to advise all parties where I intend to proceed with the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have no clue as to where you are heading.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but Mr. Ostojic, would you like the floor?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may, I'm not sure if he is completed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, of course. By all means.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. It's just not true what he says. I sent him an e-mail. He knows that this Trial Chamber is very interested in this topic. It's disingenuous to suggest and to keep playing these games. He knows what his investigator did was wrong, and he should tell the Court that right now, and I wrote him an e-mail what I thought he should do this morning to the Court, to the witnesses, and to all the lawyers here. He knows about the Orient Express restaurant. It's a long-standing restaurant. He has pictures of it. He sees plainly, clearly on its face where it's written, when it was first established. He asked the question yesterday that mischaracterized the facts by using the word "this new restaurant." I objected and I was rejected by this Court on that objection. That's misleading. The 1988 restaurant was not new. The Orient Express at Victoria Station, which is new Belgrade, which is what both witnesses have said, was in existence in 1993. They had that. I want their investigator here so that I could query whether or not he investigated it thoroughly like their other investigators or whether he uncovered this supposedly at 3 o'clock after our hearing. He shouldn't have been allowed to ask that question under any circumstances. The witness was able to say what she did on the transcript. You're invited to look at it. Mr. Gavrilovic told us yesterday, new Belgrade is where this restaurants is, not Zemun. He should bring a map on not tell us in e-mail that these are neighbourhoods next to each other. They're not neighbourhoods. They're far away from each other, Zemun and new Belgrade. He knows that. It's disingenuous, it's disrespectful, and quite frankly, it's dishonest. I'm offended. If it continues, I am going to withdraw from this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey, by way of an exception to the rule, we are giving you the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I object to the exception as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, and I am not speaking for anyone but myself on this. This kind of conduct must stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm not going to listen to this. I'm not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know, but he --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: He has an -- he doesn't need to attack me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic, please. Please. You may be able to do and behave like this in Chicago but not here, so please sit down and --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm going to make my record, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please sit down. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If he has a problem with my conduct, he can bring it with the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic, please sit down, and you will have the floor when the Trial Chamber gives it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: When I say this, Your Honour, I will say it briefly, the conduct attacking the honesty of the Prosecution must stop, and that's all I want to say. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But do you have an explanation, Mr. Thayer, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. This was what I was trying to accomplish with the Court was to let the Court know what happened yesterday afternoon to place in context what I'm going to do on cross-examination with this witness. And my concern was that that might be related to the Court's decision to bring back Gavrilovic, so I didn't want anybody to be taken by surprise if the Court had in mind certain avenues it wanted to pursue with this witness. What we did yesterday was follow up on some information that I received in the middle of my cross-examination of the current witness. The Court will recall that the prior witness, Ms. Gavrilovic, at page 24762 of the transcript, referred for the first time anywhere to the - and I'm quoting here - "Newly opened restaurant in new Belgrade that looks like a carriage of the Orient Express train. I remember that remark of his very well..." referring to the husband of the current witness. She then returned to this recollection of hers upon further cross-examination. By the way, she made the prior comment, I believe, on direct examination, and then she returned to that comment upon cross-examination yesterday morning at page 24787 of the transcript. She did remember because Toma her husband was making jokes about her failed trip on the Orient Express by saying that "there was a newly opened restaurant in our city named the Orient Express and it's decorated in the same way, and he told us to go there and imagine that we were on the trip." Again, this was new information that we had never received before that surfaced during the course, first, of the direct examination of the witness and then during Mr. McCloskey's cross. So yesterday during my cross-examination one of the investigators looked into Express, Orient Express, and what he came up with was Balkan Express and the information with which I cross-examined this witness yesterday pretty much on the fly. Following the Court session, we made further inquiries to see whether there per chance may have been other similar restaurants in Belgrade, and we discovered that there were. We discovered that there was a restaurant by the name of the Victoria Station restaurant, which is in new Belgrade, and that it is designed to look like a Victorian train carriage and so forth, and we discovered that that had been opened in 1993. We also discovered -- and this is based on one article that reviewed these three train carriage restaurants; I guess there was some effort to promote this style of dining. We discovered that there was a third restaurant that was across the river that had been open for 30 years. Based on this article, we sent out an investigator in Belgrade to interview whoever they could find at both the Victoria Station restaurant and the Balkan Ekspres restaurant to find out more information. As the Court heard yesterday with respect to the Balkan Ekspres restaurant, as it says on its own website as we saw from the sign, it was founded in 1998, and that was confirmed by the person with whom the investigator spoke. At the Victoria Restaurant location, which is also referred to as the Orient Express Restaurant on occasion, we were told that it has been open continuously since 1993. We were discovering all this information late yesterday afternoon and into the evening. Naturally, we put that into an information report late last night. I copied the article that the investigator located which discussed these three restaurants. We even downloaded a Belgrade Yellow Page page which refers to the Victoria Station restaurant as the Orient Express, and we disclosed that last night to counsel with the additional -- the new information report from our investigator which summarizes the investigative efforts that the Prosecution undertook after court yesterday and in cooperation with representatives from our field office. So all that went out as soon as we could last night so that everybody could be aware of the developments that the investigation had made. I additionally, as I mentioned, CC'd the Trial Chamber's legal officers to alert the legal officers that there was this new development given the Trial Chamber's decision to recall the prior witness. I received some criticism or questioning about my decision to do that, to send this information to the Court's legal officers. Obviously, that's not my practice. I think anybody from Chambers knows that I don't bombard Chambers with e-mails. I only CC the legal officers if it has something to do with scheduling or other administrative matters, but given this unusual situation where the Court has recalled a witness and speculating that it may have something to do with this train issue, I thought it was prudent to let the legal officers know, trusting that they would make the appropriate decision whether to pass that information on to the Trial Chamber because I know that Trial Chamber sometimes doesn't want to know everything there is to know behind a particular issue. And I think that is pretty much as much as I can summarize where we are now. And what I intend to do with the witness, and again, I've -- I have no qualms about letting everybody know, I'm simply going to tell her what happened, tell her that when I examined you yesterday I was under the impression that Balkan Ekspres restaurant was the only one in town, we found out there's another one, think it might be the one that was discussed, and see what happens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Thayer. Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't want to make a mountain out of a molehill.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I hope not.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: But could I make it clear, it was I who sent the e-mail expressing concern that the information report had been sent to the legal officers, I made it clear, first of all, that this issue didn't relate to my client; secondly, I sent it only to Mr. Thayer, Mr. McCloskey, and Mr. Krgovic, and it was a gentle inquiry, and Mr. Thayer is aware that it's an issue that I feel quite strongly about, particularly in relation to experiences I've had in other cases. Beyond that, we on behalf of General Gvero, of course not involved in this issue, but unless it's directly relevance and needed, it's our submission such material should not be sent to legal officers. But as I say, I don't want to make anything more of it. I simply think I need to admit that it was I who, I am afraid, stirred the flames of what's already quite a bitter dispute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. By the way, before I give you the floor Mr. Ostojic, I think on behalf of the Trial Chamber I better make things clear to you that we have all had extensive practice as judges or as lawyers, and we know what the boundaries are, what the limits are, what is permissible and what is not, and so does our senior legal officer. Our senior legal officer with whom we have regular meetings, and I in particular have daily meetings, knows exactly what is permissible and what is not permissible. And sometimes I am aware that he receives communications from you which he knows he ought to keep to himself and not pass on to us because it would not be regular on his part to communicate the information to us. Sometimes he asks for direction from us, but basically, basically he is a trained lawyer with much experience, and he knows where the limits are. I can put your mind at rest that if there is room for mistakes anywhere, this is certainly not one area where you can expect mistakes, neither from our side - as I said, we know what the limits are - nor from our senior legal officer. I think I ought to make that clear in the first place. Now, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MS. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours. Let me first begin by apologizing for my outburst, but these are very sensitive issues, and I do honestly from the bottom of my heart apologise for my outburst. I'm going to direct your attention to two things that my learned friend said. He says, I don't know if it's of interest to you. I'm not going to comment if it's disingenuous or not, but look on page 6 of today's transcript. He says again, which is where I get frustrated, "at the Victoria restaurant location, which is also referred to as the Orient Express restaurant on occasion." That's not true. I have to fight for this Court to hear some truth. The Orient Express Restaurant at Victoria Station has a sign that's painted on that train that says "Orient Express." Simplon Orient Express. It can be seen for blocks, several feet or metres away. They shouldn't say things like that, I believe, Your Honour. They should show the Court the picture, not the one they e-mailed us but the other one, which we can see it, where it says Victoria Station and Simplon Orient Express and clearly saying it opened in 1993. They don't want to -- that's what they should tell you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are now making the storm in the tea cup that Mr. Josse tried to avoid.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I didn't write --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we can close the issue there. Give us an opportunity to -- give me an opportunity to confer with my colleagues because, obviously, we were prepared for one thing, and we have been taken by surprise, and we'll come back to you as to what is going to happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So bottom line after all this is the following: We have agreed, the four of us, that we don't need Mrs. Gavrilovic anymore, so Madam Registrar, if you could make -- communicate this to her and apologise to her for any inconvenience and, again, wish her a safe journey back to Belgrade and maybe a nice evening out at the Orient Express. The other thing is this, that, also, it's a bottom line and thinking with hindsight, all this, all this could have been avoided had your witness summaries, Mr. Ostojic, been more excessive or comprehensive. The restaurant could have been mentioned in the witness summaries; investigations could have been taken -- been made before and ... but anyway, leave it, leave it. Let's continue with the witness, the current witness. If you could usher her in, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, Mr. Cubbon just asked me about that witness in the videolink. I've had a chance to look at a translated medical report, and then we've translated the medical terms, and we won't be objecting to the videolink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So in fact, I was working on that this morning. There are arrangements already going on to have the videolink testimony conducted on the 9th and 10th of September. Our staff can confirm to the registrar that the motion is being granted here and now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, madam.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Welcome back. We are going to continue with your testimony and hopefully finish soon. You are still testifying under oath as per your solemn undertaking yesterday. Mr. Thayer will continue and conclude with his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good morning again, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I want to pick up on a topic that we touched on yesterday, and that has to do with the discussion that you recall about the Orient Express and this restaurant in a train car. Do you recall talking about that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall that there was some mention, you thought it might have been from one of the Gavrilovics, about a newly opened restaurant that was made like a train car for people to eat in; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't recall that. I don't think I heard them say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What do you recall, then, hearing, or what do you recall hearing them say?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was some discussion about the Orient Express, about taking a travel on board of the train because of their anniversary, and they said that they would go but had no money. They were supposed to travel to a large city such as London, Paris. As far as I can tell from Belgrade, the Orient Express did not run at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I just want to turn your attention back to what you said yesterday, ma'am. You answered that, "Yes, I heard it being mentioned that evening, the Orient Express and the train car," and then I asked you: "The train car restaurant you are referring to", and you said: "Yes, I mean the restaurant." Do you recall saying that yesterday, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not say anything about the restaurant. I did not even know that the restaurant existed. You asked me and you showed me a picture of the restaurant. I never went to that restaurant. I don't know where it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's right, and you certainly told us that yesterday, ma'am. What I'm asking you is, when we spoke yesterday I asked you - and this is at page 24854 of the transcript - "Do you remember during the course of this second dinner, or maybe even during the course of the first dinner, do you remember during the dinner joking about the Orient Express? Do you remember somebody saying something to the effect of, 'Well, there's this new restaurant that looks like a train car. Since you can't go on the real Orient Express, maybe you could go have dinner in the train car'?" I asked you, do you remember any conversation or discussion along those lines, and then you answered: "Yes, I heard it being mentioned that evening, the Orient Express and the train car." And then I asked you: "The train car restaurant you are referring to?" And you answered, and this is at line 24: "Yes, I mean the restaurant." And then I asked you: "I know this is going back, but can you recall who came up with the joke about the train car restaurant? If you don't remember, that's fine. If you remember, please share that with the Trial Chamber." And your answer was, and this is on the next page, 24855, line 3: "I don't remember. As I said a moment ago, I was going in and out of the room where we were, going back to the kitchen to bring out drinks and food. Maybe I was absent at that very moment when someone said it. Perhaps it was one of the Gavrilovics." Do you remember saying that yesterday, ma'am? We need an audible answer, ma'am, one that we can hear, a yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you stand by that answer?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I would like, Mr. Thayer, for you to read the -- read up the answer which appears in page 24851, lines from 16 to 18. If you could find it, where she said: "Well, it seems I'll have to take you by your hands to take you to the train station, and at least you can look at the train. That was the tone of the evening."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you stand by that recollection as well, ma'am, or is your recollection now different?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stand by that recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So then, ma'am, just to follow up on His Honour's question, is it your recollection that there were jokes of both kinds made that night, one by Mr. Beara about taking you down to look at the train and another joke by one of the Gavrilovics about instead of going on your trip, going to this newly opened restaurant in a train car?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, those were the jokes about all that, about the situation, and we had quite a few laughs about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Ma'am, we did a little bit of checking around yesterday after court and we found another restaurant, also in Belgrade, and it's called Victoria Station. Sometimes it's referred to as the "Orient Express Restaurant." And to be fair with you, when I asked you the question yesterday about the Balkan Ekspres restaurant, I was under the impression that that was the only such restaurant in Belgrade. But it turns out there might be -- in fact, there is more than one such restaurant in Belgrade. So what I want to do is give you an opportunity to look at some pictures, read some portions of an article, look at another document, and see if that helps your recollection, changes your recollection at all about this issue of whether the restaurant and the train that was referred to was one place or another, okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter 3649, please. Your Honours, I think everything should be uploaded in e-court by now, including the English translation of one of the articles which is attached to this information report. So I'm going to skip the actual text of the report, obviously. I just want to show the witness in her own language, and this is at page 3 of the document, an article.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Ma'am, there's going to be an article appearing on your computer screen, and it's going to show a train carriage and then in one photograph at the top and then on the bottom photograph it will show some restaurant booths. Just tell us when you see that document.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see the pictures, but I'm not familiar with the place. I was never in this restaurant. I don't even know where it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's fine. The article says that the restaurant Victoria Station is in Novi Grad, and can we go to page 6, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think -- I think now you've covered enough terrain to prompt us to say that we've heard enough on this now, and you can move.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Great. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can move to something else. I mean, it's clear enough now. I don't think we need any further explanations from the witness. Yes, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: My computer has frozen, so if I can just have some technical assistance with the files.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which -- you have only got that one. Yes. Yeah, I'll attend to that straightaway. Madam Registrar. Shall we move on in the meantime, or do you prefer to stop?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think we can move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Anyone else with the same problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I just adjusted it somehow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, you testified that you first met with the Beara Defence team in February of 2008 at Nada Beara's home; is that correct? That was at transcript 24830.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how is it that you are sure of that month?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was this year towards the end of February when Mr. Milan Stanic arrived from The Hague. Maybe a few days before that I came to visit Nada. That's where I found Mr. Milan Stanic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. You told us yesterday that you were visiting with Nada Beara and then Mr. Stanic arrived. Is that how it happened? Were you visiting with Ms. Beara and then Mr. Stanic arrived?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there may be a confusion there. In any case, this is where I met him and this is where I saw him. Now, as to who came first, who came later, I may have been mistaken about that, but this is where I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And that meeting may have lasted as long as two hours, correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know, we did not time this meeting. I don't know if it was two hours, two hours and a quarter, or two hours and a half. I wouldn't know. I wouldn't be able to tell you how long the meeting lasted.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what did he tell you he wanted?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We chatted. We had a lengthy conversation. He asked me how well and since when I knew the Beara family, when I first met them, whether we socialized a lot, whether we were friends, and so on and so forth. I inquired after Mr. Beara, his health, and that's the general outline of the conversation that we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did he ask you at that time if you were interested in being a witness?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And was Nada Beara present for this entire meeting that you had with Mr. Stanic?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, she was.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So she certainly knew at that point that you were a potential witness, correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, she did know, but she could not be certain whether I would follow through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Do you still have the problem, or do you have the problem again, Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I do have the problem again, but we can continue. I just wanted to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, just -- because I saw you making signs. I just wanted to verify that. We still need technical assistance for Mr. Ostojic, please. Thank you. Sorry, Mr. Thayer. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And was anyone taking notes during this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did anyone ask you to write anything down?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody did.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you testified yesterday that after the indictment against Mr. Beara was made public, you read about it in the newspapers. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you also told us yesterday that you haven't been following the trial closely, but you do see TV or read press coverage about the trial from time to time; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So even though you've probably never seen the indictment - forget about reading the indictment - in this case, at the time you met with Mr. Stanic in February of 2008, you knew then that this case was generally about what happened after the fall of Srebrenica. Isn't that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not familiar with the details of all this. I only know as much as I have read in the papers and seen on TV on the news. This is as much as I know, and this is as much I am familiar with this Srebrenica case.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So you certainly know this is about what happened after the VRS took over Srebrenica? Even though you may not know individual counts or facts there are alleged, you know that this trial has to do with what happened after the VRS took over Srebrenica, correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, I don't know that much. There is not much I can tell you save for what I've read or seen on TV. As for the details, I really wouldn't be able to say anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, when you met with Mr. Stanic in February of 2008 and sat with him for the two hours, you knew that it was important for you to be as complete and as accurate as you could be, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you tell him everything you could remember at the time in 2008 in February?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we did not have that much time, so we could not go into the greatest of details.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, in those two hours in February, did you talk about July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we just touched upon the subject of July and how things were at the time. But as I say, I don't know much because I have never followed the developments in Republika Srpska that closely.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: My question more specifically is, in that two hours or maybe even more, as you said, that you spent with Mr. Stanic, did he ask you about your recollection about events in July 1995? Not generally what was happening, not what the VRS was doing, but did he ask you questions in February of 2008 about what you were doing and your recollections of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We did not discuss anything concrete on that particular occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Where and when was the next time you met with anyone from the Beara Defence team?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met with Mr. Stanic somewhat later, maybe a month later. Actually, we spoke on the phone, but we met sometime in mid-April.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what did he want at that meeting, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, then we spoke about things, and then he asked me how much I remember from the month of July 1995 and what I remembered.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And again, you knew it was important when he was asking you these questions about July of 1995 to be as complete and as accurate as possible?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I knew it was important, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And during this meeting, was anyone taking any notes?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were just Mr. Stanic and I.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you observe him taking any notes or writing anything down at any time or recording anything with a machine?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was actually taking notes, yes. Mr. Stanic was.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how long was this meeting, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe an hour or so or maybe just over an hour, an hour and a quarter.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So when was the first time that you told anyone from the Beara Defence team about the events in 1995, these two dinners, for example, that you've told us about over the last day or so. When was the first time you told anybody from the Defence team for Mr. Beara about those events?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was during my second meeting with Mr. Stanic in mid-April. I can't remember the exact date. I don't know whether it was on the 18th, the 19th, or the 20th of April, but it was about that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you have to consult anything or refer to anything during the course of this meeting to help jog your recollection about these events, or were you able simply to remember everything from your mind?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we started by saying that the times were very hard in 1994 and 1995. In 1995, my late husband lost his job. Living was not easy. The financial situations became more difficult, and that's how the conversation started. That's how I started telling him the story, and that's how I shared with him whatever I've been sharing with you these two days.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. But certainly, he was very interested in what you had to say about these two dinners that you had with the Bearas and this particular time period; isn't that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, but in order to arrive at all that we mentioned many other things that were happening during the years after the break-up of our state. This is how the conversation started. We were talking about people losing jobs, about life being very hard. We basically spoke in general terms, and then I continued speaking about the specific events that happened and that Mr. Stanic was particularly interested in.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what were the specific events that happened that Mr. Stanic was particularly interested in?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that Mr. Stanic was interested in our get-togethers with Ljubisa Beara. He asked me when I saw him, when I spoke to him, and that's what I told him.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you made it clear yesterday that you didn't even know Mr. Beara was having his birthday until Nada Beara told you so?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you said -- and let me just take you back a little bit to what you said yesterday, and then I'll put my question to you, but I want to give you a little bit of background of what you've said. You said referring to the dinner at the restaurant, which my friend referred to as the first dinner, that you stayed there until 11 to 1130. Then Nada Beara told you, and I'm quoting from the transcript yesterday: "Do you know what happens tomorrow?" And you replied: "Not really." And then she told you that the next day was her husband's birthday. That's the first thing you said. And a little bit later, you testified in 1995, and I'm quoting here: "We got together in July when Ljubisa was in Belgrade. That was the day when we went to the restaurant; and then Nada reminded me that on the following day, which was I think the 14th of July -- because this is what she told me. Otherwise, I wouldn't have known." Okay, and that's at transcript 24841 of yesterday's hearing. The previous quote was from 24833. Now, in answer to a question from His Honour, the Presiding Judge, you said -- or the question was: "At the time, were you aware of Mr. Beara's date of birth or birthday?" And you replied, "When we got together on that first evening while we were sitting and chatting, or rather, when it was time for us to go home..." You told the Trial Chamber then that Nada Beara told you that Ljubisa Beara's birthday was the next day, and I'm quoting again: "That's when she told me the date. Otherwise, I wouldn't have known." That's the end of your quote there at 24842 of the transcript. So ma'am, let me see if I understand what you're telling the Trial Chamber. You are at this restaurant. Nada Beara tells you, do you know what tomorrow is. You say, no, I don't. She says, it's Ljubisa's birthday. And then she goes out of her way to tell you that the next day is the 14th of July. She actually gives you the date. She goes out of her way to give you the date of 14th of July. Is that what you're telling the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it was. That was our conversation when we met that evening and when we were supposed to go home. That was on the 13th, and then Nada told me that on the following day was her husband's birthday, which I wouldn't have known had she not specifically mentioned the fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So ma'am, how is it that 13 years later here you can recall that exact date that Nada Beara gave you that night at the restaurant, that exact date of 14 July as opposed to any other date? How is it that 14th of July sticks out in your mind?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in the month of May when we got together and when we socialised at our house, at the house of me and my late husband was the 16th of May, and it was my birthday on that day. Ljubisa and Nada were there, and then we met on several occasions after that, and in the month of July we also socialised and got together. And I would not have known that it was either the 13th or 14th if Nada hadn't mentioned that, which means that the day before we were together, which was on the 13th, I would not have known that it was the 13th. I would not be so sure. It could have been the 12th or the 11th, but I knew that it was on the 13th because when we were saying our good-byes then she said, tomorrow my old man - that's how she referred to her husband - celebrates his birthday. And that's how I remember things. It could have been some other date in July as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: My question to you, ma'am, is, how can you explain to the Trial Chamber how that date, the 14th of July, has stuck in the your memory for the last 13 years as opposed to July 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th, so on and so on, because you didn't know Ljubisa Beara's birthday. You've told us that consistently. So why is it -- can you tell the Court why is it that that date has stuck in your mind since you didn't know when his birthday was?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if someone tells me something, then I remember things. It hasn't been so long a time ago. I maybe even made a note somewhere so as to know that it was Ljubisa's birthday. I was born in May, my late husband in June. That's how I generally try to remember things.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So you think you might have a note somewhere, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could be. I wasn't going back to my notes, but when Mr. Stanic and I spoke he asked me whether I remembered, and it brought back things.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: He asked you whether you remembered what, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He asked me when we saw each other, when we socialised, when we spent time together. That would be it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you know that Svetlana Gavrilovic has met with the Beara team investigators, correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when did you first learn this?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly when Mr. Stanic contacted Svetlana. I didn't ask her that, she didn't tell me that. Whether it was after our conversation, well, I can't say. I didn't ask her. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So I'm a little confused about your last answer, ma'am. Is it your testimony that you and Ms. Gavrilovic have never spoken to each other about either her meeting, and we'll start with her meeting with Mr. Stanic.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did talk about it, but I didn't ask her on what day it was, whether it was two or three days after our meeting or a week later. I didn't ask her that. However, I do know that they spoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you and Ms. Gavrilovic share with each other at any time what you told Mr. Stanic?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't go into any details. We were trying to remember what was happening that July 1995, and then she said, well, that was the year my late husband and myself celebrated our anniversary. That's what we could recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So that's what you two recall together as you were talking about what Mr. Stanic had spoken about with Ms. Gavrilovic. Is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know what the two of them talked about. When we met and talked a few days after, she told me that. She reminded me, saying that it was a date that one remembers.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So she gave you that date; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, she said so.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what did she tell you about her recollection of the events of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't discuss that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So it's your testimony that you and Ms. Gavrilovic never talked to each other about, for example, the two dinners that you told my friend about and that you've spoken to the Trial Chamber about? You never spoke about those two dinners with Ms. Gavrilovic in the last few months?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. We talked about things in general but without any details. I didn't ask her what specifically she talked about with Mr. Stanic and the other way around. She didn't ask me, either.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, if we could have 65 ter 3631, please. Now, ma'am, we don't have a translation of this, so I'm just going to read something to you. In April of this year, we received a summary of what your testimony was going to be from the Beara Defence team, and I just want to read it to you - it shouldn't take too long - and ask you some questions. The summary says that - and this is referring to you, ma'am - "Witness has been a friend of Beara family since 1975..." and I understand that that's a typo. It should be 1985.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: "And they socialised quite frequently after the Bearas moved to Belgrade in 1991. After Beara joined the VRS, they would see each other whenever he happened to be in Belgrade. Their socialisation consisted almost entirely of home visits with a single exception when they went out to a restaurant at the insistence of the witness's spouse, and that was for Beara's birthday. She recalls that that was in 1995 because that was the first time she and her husband did not vacation on the sea coast due to financial problems. Since her husband had commitments the night of Beara's birthday, they went out for dinner with the Bearas the evening before that. They went to the Cuburska lipa restaurant on 14th of December Street. The following evening, Nada and Ljubisa Beara came to visit the witness at her house. Also in attendance were friends Svetlana Gavrilovic and late husband Djordje." Now, ma'am, the summary I just read to you contains no references to any dates of these two dinners. My question is, when you met with the Beara team's investigators either in February or in April, did you give them any dates of these dinners?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And I see here that there's no reference to any Orient Express or train restaurant stories or even mention. In your meetings with the Beara Defence team in February or April, did you tell them about your recollections concerning the Gavrilovics' anniversary plans that fell through and the Orient Express trip that they had planned and the jokes about taking somebody to the train station for Mr. Beara or the joke about going to the train restaurant? Did you say any of that to the investigators in February or April of 2008?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't discuss that with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: May we have 65 ter 3630, please. Ma'am, we asked for some more information from Mr. Beara's lawyers about what your testimony was likely to be, and we received another summary, and I'm just going to read the new information. The summary consists of what I've just read to you a few moments ago and then some new information. So let me just read to you this additional paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt. In light of Mr. -- my learned friend's question on page 26, line 16, I think it's fair to this witness to tell her, also, the date of this summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Page 26, line 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yeah. He said the first exhibit that he used, he said in April of this year, and I think it would only be fair if he tells her when this summary was provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Fair enough I think, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We asked for some more information. And then this summary was supplied to us in August of 2008. Now, the new information is: "In addition to the foregoing" -- and that's referring to your earlier statement -- or the earlier summary, I'm sorry -- "it was clarified with the witness Cekic that her and her late husband had dinner with the Bearas on the 13th July, 1995, because they were unable to attend the luncheon party Ms. Beara had for Ljubisa Beara at the Beara's house, which she had on the 14 July 1995. Later that same evening on 14 July, 1995, the Cekics and Bearas again get together at Cekic's home. During the visit at the Cekics' house on the 14 July, the Gavrilovic family, Svetlana and her husband Djordje, were also present, and the gathering lasted approximately two to three hours. The witness does not recall what they specifically ate that evening but assumes that they served them the traditional pita and homemade cookies. Finally, Ms. Cekic informed us that her late husband and her late husband have worked together in the past in the company Beojadro and Splitjadro. It was through that professional working relationship that they became friends. Ms. Cekic will testify as to Ljubisa Beara's good character and physical appearance as well as his dialect." Now, this new summary includes some specific dates on which you say these events happened. You told us a few moments ago that you didn't provide any dates in your other interviews. Tell us how the dates came up in this interview. How is it that we are now seeing exact dates in August of 2008 when you didn't provide them in April or previously?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably did say that. If Mr. Stanic was following me, then it should be in here. When we met at the restaurant, I don't -- I couldn't remember exactly what the date was, but as we were parting our ways, Nada stressed that the 14th of July was Ljubisa Beara's birthday; therefore, the evening before when we were together was the 13th. That's it. That's what I could recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. My question is, though, ma'am -- you didn't recall those dates in your April 30th meeting with the investigator, and my question is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think he just may have misspoken. I don't think that she said there was a April 30th meeting. She gave specific dates, actually, which was mid-April. The filing was pursuant to the Court's order for May 1st, but just not to confuse the case, there was no meeting on April 30th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. You are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I stand corrected. Your April. We'll just leave it as your --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Why don't we say mid-April or the dates that she gave when she said the 18th, 19th, or 20th?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, your recollection, what you've just told the Chamber, if I understand you correctly, is there were no dates in that April summary that I just read because you didn't mention any dates in April when you met with the investigator; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I can tell you that I may have mentioned the dates, but Mr. Stanic had not had noted them down. Later on when I was trying to recall all of it, I was able to remember those things, and I may have added that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So the fact is, you can't be sure whether you were able to recall those dates in April of 2008 when you met with the investigator. Isn't that correct, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do recall that, but as I'm trying to tell you it could be that Mr. Stanic hadn't taken note of it. Maybe there was an omission, something I can't explain. I can't tell you what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. So let me just be clear. What is your recollection as to whether you were able to provide these dates of the 13th and 14th of July during your meeting in April with Mr. Stanic? Did you or did you not provide him the dates on that occasion? And if you can't recall, ma'am, that's fine too.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I said, I probably remembered that subsequently, maybe the next time we met or heard each other over the phone. Mr. Stanic, I remember, was later absent because of health reasons. As for why he hadn't written it down, I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And in the additional summary from August that I've just read, there's no -- again, no mention of any 25th wedding anniversary, jokes about the Orient Express, or anything about a restaurant or a train. Do you recall telling the investigators or anybody from the Beara Defence team about those topics when you met in August?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that. I only tried to explain the extent of the discussions, jokes, when we were at our house the next day, the 14th of July. But as for any details, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, you just told us that you "tried to explain the extent of the discussions and the jokes when we were at our house the next day, the 14th of July." So my question is, if that's what you were trying to do in August, how come we don't see that in the additional summary? Is it because you didn't recall it in August; is it because you said it but it wasn't written down; or is there some other explanation, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought that it wasn't ... I thought I was supposed to say what we were talking about, what we were making jokes about, and it's probably for that reason why I didn't share that with the investigators.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Ma'am, I'm sorry. I just don't understand your last answer. Maybe it's my problem this morning. But you just said: "I thought I was supposed to say what we were talking about, what we were making jokes about, and it's probably for that reason why I didn't share that with the investigators." My question to you is --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I do think at this point Mr. Ostojic may have missed, as we see on the transcript, the beginning part of her answer, and I think maybe he can read that to her. I think the translators didn't pick up on what she said specifically, and also, just so that I can remember, and I apologise, I'm going to have a look at page 31, line 16. I don't know that that was accurately translated, but we'll deal with that at a later time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to help you there. If someone else who speaks the language can be of assistance. In what sense do you think ...

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We'll listen the tape, but I think she said "I didn't" in reference to that, not that I don't know because she said it rather plainly, but we'll take a look at it just to be sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Thank you. Yes, yes, yes. It can be verified later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, back to my question, ma'am. You just testified that "I thought I was supposed to say what we were talking about, what we were making jokes about, and it's probably for that reason why I didn't share that with the investigators." Now, I just -- when you met with the Beara Defence team in August of 2008, did you or did you not tell them about the jokes about the Orient Express vacation or holiday that fell through, the 25th anniversary gift that the Gavrilovics wanted to have for themselves, that trip, jokes about the -- going to the train station that Mr. Beara made, or the joke about having dinner in a train restaurant? Did you or did you not in August of 2008 share that information with the Beara Defence team?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that my late husband was out of work, that we were unable to go on a vacation as we had done before, that we were very sorry about it, that we remained in Belgrade, that we socialised, that we saw the Beara and Gavrilovic families, that there were jokes, stories, and whatnot, and I also said that at our house when we saw each other on the evening of the 14th that I had prepared a pie, which is a traditional meal, cakes, ham, drinks. In the meantime I went to the kitchen, and we were talking about this and that. If I had made an omission in the fact that I may not have mentioned to the Defence the fact about the Orient Express, I don't know. But as for the rest, I stand by what I said. I tried to explain what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, you and Ms. Gavrilovic have certainly shared that story between you, that joke about the Orient Express and going to the train station, the joke that Mr. Beara made, and the joke that one of the Gavrilovics made about going to a train restaurant. You and Ms. Gavrilovic have shared those jokes, haven't you, since this night that you say was July 14th of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We spoke within the context of jokes because at the time nobody had any money to travel and they didn't, either, because as far as I can remember and as far as I can actually be sure of, that train did not have its departure point in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And since being contacted by the Beara Defence team in February of 2008, you and Ms. Gavrilovic have spoken to each other and recalled these jokes about Mr. Beara saying he will take somebody down to the train station, or instead of going on the Orient Express, we'll go to a train restaurant; isn't that true, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we spoke about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I see it's time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. We'll have a 25-minute break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer, if you could conclude, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I will, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Ma'am, you just told us before the break that after you had been contacted by the Beara Defence team in 2008, sometime after that you and Ms. Gavrilovic had spoken to each other and recalled these jokes about the train restaurant, going down to the train station, the Orient Express. My question is, did you have that conversation, or if it was more than one conversation, did you have one of those conversations before you spoke to the Beara team in April or after you spoke to the Beara team in April?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not before. We never discussed that before.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall whether you had one of those conversations before your meeting with the Beara Defence team in August, or was it after your meeting in August?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not talk about that before August, either, before we met with the Defence team. We never discussed that before.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So can you tell the Trial Chamber when you had this discussion or this conversation or conversations, if it's more than one, with Ms. Gavrilovic where you recalled the jokes about the Orient Express or eating in a train restaurant?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we saw each other after the meeting with the Defence team, we reminisced on what had happened, what we had talked about that evening, how we joked about things, how we'd chatted and socialised, and in more general terms what it was that people or friends talk about when they get together.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So you are telling the Trial Chamber that after you met with the Defence team in August of 2008, you and Ms. Gavrilovic had a conversation where the two of you talked about the train restaurant and going down to the train station? That happened sometime after your meeting in August of 2008; you and Ms. Gavrilovic talked about that together, correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We chatted and one of the things that we touched upon was that story, as well, and that was after the meeting with the Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And then when you came here, you met with the Defence team again, and you were proofed; that is, somebody met with you to discuss your upcoming testimony, and this would have been sometime in the last few days, correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And during that proofing session, did you tell the Beara Defence team anything about this Orient Express trip or the train restaurant or Mr. Beara taking somebody down to the train station? Did you tell the Beara Defence team anything about those events, those recollections that you and Ms. Gavrilovic talked about together in August?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I spoke to the Defence team, I told them what had been going on, how life had been, and we also discussed the two relevant days, the 13th and the 14th of July. We also spoke about Ljubisa, his family, about our friendship. I told them that they were a wonderful family, very normal, very stable, with two very good and healthy children. This is more or less what we talked about, and as for the jokes that we shared that evening at my home, I did not say anything specific about any of those to the Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you didn't mention the train restaurant jokes or that topic until I asked you about it here in court, and you remembered it. Were you able to remember it, recall it so quickly because you had had this recent conversation in August with Ms. Gavrilovic, or did someone tell you about it during the course of one of the interviews you had with the Beara team, whether it was a proofing session or an interview? Can you tell the Court?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not discuss that with the Defence team. We only discussed the things that I have just mentioned. As for Svetlana she said that, and then when you asked me, I remember what we had talked about that evening, what kind of jokes had been exchanged, and I actually remembered those because they did make an impact.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And they made an impact, but your testimony is you didn't tell the Beara Defence team about those topics; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not getting your drift at all. What is it that you are asking me?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, you just told the Court that as a result of your conversation with Ms. Gavrilovic you actually remembered those jokes about the train station and the train restaurant because they made an impact. My question is, if they made an impact, why didn't you tell the Beara Defence team?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the issue never came up. Mr. Beara's Defence team asked me about the character of Mr. Ljubisa Beara, his family, how I had met them, how we had socialised, how often we'd seen each other, and this is more or less what we discussed. And then when you asked me about the other thing, that's when I remembered it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Ma'am, clearly, the Beara Defence team spoke with you at some point about these events that you say happened in July of 1995, these two dinners. You've told us about that. My question is, isn't it the case that you didn't recall these events in your conversations because it was Ms. Gavrilovic who told you about those events?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, she did talk about the events that had happened before, but that's why -- we are friends. That's why we socialised, to exchange our everyday life about the good and the bad that is happening to us. I believe that's what friends are for. That's what acquaintances are for. I really don't know what else I could add to that. What else do you expect me to tell you?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: One more question on this topic, ma'am. After February of 2008, were you and Ms. Gavrilovic and Ms. -- and Nada Beara, did you ever get together or were you ever together after any time after February of 2008 and discuss any of these things that Mr. Stanic talked to you and to Ms. Gavrilovic about, these events of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Svetlana and I, as I've already told you, did reminisce on that and spoke about that, but Nada never wanted to participate in such conversations, and we never spoke about the events with her. But we did remind each other of how we socialised that evening and what happened on that particular evening, but we never shared any of our conversations with the Defence, with Nada, or at least I never did. I don't know about the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I want to turn your attention to your testimony about getting together with the Bearas on your birthday in May of 1995, and I just want to quote back to you what you said about that occasion, and this is on page 24832 of the transcript, and I quote: "Since in May there's my birthday. On that day Ljubisa was in Belgrade. I invited both him and Nada to come over, not for the sake of the birthday but simply to sit down and chat." Now, when in May 1995 did you learn that Mr. Beara was in town?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know. I can't tell you when. I don't know when Mr. Beara came to Belgrade, but on that day in May - and I can't remember what day it was exactly - in any case, on the 16th of May he was there, and Nada and him came to our house to have a chat, to have a drink and a piece of cake. I'd baked a birthday cake to mark the occasion, and Ljubisa and Nada brought me a golden charm depicting an anchor because this is something that has sea references, and as you know, Mr. Ljubisa Beara is a soldier -- or soldier who served at the sea.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So just to be clear, your recollection is that this get-together was on the actual date of your birthday, 16 May 1995? Sorry, we just need audible answer for the record, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, is there anything that stands out in your memory that might help you recall how long Mr. Beara had been in Belgrade at the time you got together on that occasion, and if it helps at all, that was a Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you how long.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you have any idea where he was in the days before he came over to celebrate your birthday?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, yesterday I asked you the following question: "Following the memorial service for your husband in 2001, when do you recall speaking with Ljubisa Beara?" And your answer was, "Well, we met in the year 2000 while my husband was still alive. That was in the month of June. We went to visit Ljubisa and Nada. Ljubisa always liked to surprise us and organise a barbecue because he had been living for many years in Split and he used to speak in the Split dialect." Now, I asked you a simple question about 2001, and you responded about 2000 and talked about a barbecue, and then you went on to say that he spoke in a Split dialect. Ma'am, my question to you is who told you that it was important to tell the Trial Chamber that Mr. Beara spoke in a Split dialect?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I object to the form of the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I can rephrase.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think it's the case, and the transcript in any case is misleading. Mr. Ostojic didn't give his okay to the form of the question. He objected to it. Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Ma'am, did anyone tell you that it was important to tell the Trial Chamber that Mr. Beara spoke in a Split dialect?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody told me that. This is simply the way Ljubisa speaks, and it was rather odd to hear it in Serbia because people in Serbia speak the way I do, for example, and Ljubisa had his very specific and strong dialect on account of the fact that he had lived and worked in Split.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So when you happened to mention that to the Trial Chamber yesterday, that was just a spontaneous statement on your part; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, going back to these two dinners that you have told the Trial Chamber about, did Ms. Gavrilovic ever tell you that the dinner at your house that you say you hosted for the Bearas for his birthday, did she ever tell you that the date of that event was July 14th?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, she didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: She has never told you that; is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAVA CEKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She didn't tell me that. Ms. Gavrilovic never told me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Thayer. Is there re-examination, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Cekic, we've come to the end of your testimony. We have no further questions for you, which means you are free to go. You'll be assisted by our staff. On behalf of the Trial Chamber, I wish to thank you for having come over to give testimony, and I also wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ostojic, do you have any documents, any exhibits to tender?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We do have, Your Honour, the Exhibit with the Orient Express on the Victoria Station, 1993 restaurant, but I think we may cover that in a separate motion. I know I didn't show to any of -- or the witness, but that came up last night when we looked for it in the internet, and we -- they have a couple documents that they put into e-court. The picture isn't clear. We have a clearer picture of where it says Orient Express on the train in new Belgrade, but we may deal with that subsequently. I just don't know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's up to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I can produce it. I have it. We can produce it. I think we were going to call it ...

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm sorry. If it makes any difference, we have no objection to that -- those exhibits coming in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. That being so -- thank you, Mr. Thayer. That being so, Mr. Ostojic, I suppose you can tender them now.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It's only one Exhibit, and it's 2D600, actually, from what I recall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there any objection from any of the other Defence teams? None. Mr. Thayer, do you have any documents to tender?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We do, Mr. President. We have 65 ter number 3629. That is the information report which we referenced yesterday and showed a couple of attachments through. 3630 and 3631, those are 65 ter summaries. In fact, I've read, I believe, most of those in, so actually as I'm looking at it we can withdraw that unless there's no objection in which case throw them in, we've got them marked, but I do recognise I read those in, and they are a matter of record, anyway. And then we have 3649, which is the information report that we cranked out last night referred to today along with the attachments that we put up before the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Mr. Ostojic, any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I do. I do object to 3629 and 3649. It's an information report, I know, but I think that it's misleading for the Court to have it. I think, with all due respect, if they want to have the investigator come in and he can share with us his process. I don't think for our point we need it, but we do object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you wish to respond to that, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's a matter that was of some discussion. It's -- we'll leave it in the Court's hands as to whether the Chamber feels that it needs to have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Our decision is as follows: We consider it to have -- all these documents to have some importance for the integrity of the evidence that was adduced and heard in relation to the subject matter that you are aware of, so these documents are admitted. Any objection to the other documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I should have said that, but yeah, I mean, I don't think it's necessary. We filed the 65 ter summary. They are the same. The Court has it, so I would just as a formality object to those two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, the summaries are -- the summaries, even Mr. Thayer himself factually explained that it's neither here nor there because he did read them out in court in any case.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think that's all the documents, so no other --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. Do you insist on having them admitted or not, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Not at all, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Then leave them, forget them. I wouldn't know the reference number now offhand, but we certainly know what we're talking about, though, which ones we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So these are not being tendered, and we don't have to discuss them any further. All right. Can we have the next witness, please, who will be Mr. Kerkez, no?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, to you, Mr. Kerkez.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And you're welcome to these proceedings. You have been summoned as a witness by the Defence team for Ljubisa Beara. Before you start giving evidence, you need to make a solemn declaration that you will be testifying the truth, the contents of which is being handed to you now. Please read it out aloud, and that will be your solemn undertaking with us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Kerkez. Please make yourself comfortable.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic will go first, who will then be followed on cross-examination by others. Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Ostojic:

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. As you know, my name is John Ostojic, and I'm one of the attorneys who represents Ljubisa Beara. Can you please for the record state your full name?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: My name is Milan Kerkez.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. Kerkez, so that we can have a better understanding of you the person, can you give us your date of birth and place of birth, please?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I was born on the 5th of February, 1978, in Belgrade, in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And sir, can you share with us your educational background, such as what's the highest level of education that you attained?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I am a university graduate in economics obtained from the Belgrade School of Business Administration, which means I have a bachelors degree, and my official title after graduation is the manager of small and mid-sized companies.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And just give us the year, if you will, of when you graduated.
