utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: It was in December 2007, and before that I obtained an associate degree after attended a school for two years and graduating in 2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Are you currently employed, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I am employed, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you share with us where?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: In the Alpha Bank in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you for that information. Let's talk about the Bearas. Do you know the Beara family?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes, I do, through my friend Branko Beara. I have known him since the 7th grade when he arrived from Split. We were classmates at elementary school, and we are still friends. We visit each other's families, we go out together, and for awhile we played handball together while we were in high school. We used to hang out much more than we do now because now we have more obligations on our hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you ever go on a vacation with Branko Beara?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes, I did, but only one summer. We have known each other for a long time, but we spent only one summer together, which was in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And I know you brought some pictures with you with respect to that, and we are grateful for that. We'll get to that in a little bit. How do you remember the year being 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I remember it because there are five of us friends who have been together since the primary school, and that was the only summer that all of us spent together. During the previous years and after that, we did spend summers together, but it was never all five of us in one place together.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall where you went on this summer vacation -- or this vacation in 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Of course. Since the year before, that year, and the next year, I was in Petrovac. I spent my summer three years in a row in a the same house with the same people. That summer we were in Petrovac as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And just tell us where Petrovac is.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Petrovac is on the Montenegrin coast some 50 kilometres away from Budva, Budva being the closest bigger town.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember, sir, when you went on vacation with Branko Beara and others in Petrovac?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: It was between the 16th of July and the 31st of July. Since I was a kid, I spent my vacation with parents during -- between those two dates with my parents, and I used to play handball, and by that time I would always have to go back to Belgrade to start my handball preparations for the next season. That particular summer, I was the one organising the vacation.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: When does the handball preparations commence?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: The 1st of August, every 1st of August. I was playing handball there -- then at the Studentski Grad Handball Club as did Branko Beara, and our coach used the system which meant that every 1st of August we had to go back. We were still kids at the time, and we were practicing for the senior team, and it would not have been good for our career to be late for the preparations.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. Kerkez, I'm just waiting because we are getting a simultaneous translation so that everyone can follow along with your testimony. Sir, I'm going to try to take you slowly through this period. Do you remember how you came or what mode of transportation you took to Petrovac?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: You mean what mode of transport, or -- we were on a bus. On the 15th in the evening, we set off from the sports centre hall at Banjica. I can even tell you what the transport company was that we used. It was the cheapest way to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What was it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: It's called the BS Tours. I still think they offer the cheapest fare even today.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, do you remember whether or not on the 15th of July prior to taking this BS Tours bus to Petrovac whether or not you had met with Branko Beara or any of the other individuals who were going on this summer vacation in Petrovac?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I did. We planned that summer together as of the last day of school that year, and we agreed that all five of us would go. We decided that we would go to Petrovac, and I got in touch with the lady whose phone number I already had. Branko was short of cash, and it wasn't sure whether he would be able to go. Therefore, in early July I reserved a room for four with the lady with a potential fifth person on an additional bed. On the last day, basically, the 14th of July, Branko asked us to come to his house and he said that he had the money. I rang the lady and I told her, well, it seems there will be five of us after all. Then we bought the bus tickets and took off.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you see Branko Beara on the 14th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Of course, at his house. He invited us.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness will have to repeat all the names he said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Branko invited us to come over to tell us THAT he had the money, and he just wanted to know who would take the frisbee, the ball, some food, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. Kerkez, and I apologise, but I speak very fast, and they have trouble usually with me. But you've just said the names of the other individuals, and can you just please kindly repeat them for us so that we can have it in the transcript. We were unable to get their names when you said them.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes. We met at Branco's place. He invited us. Boris and Emil Cukic were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I think it's Boris, right? B-O-R-I-S, I think we had it, and those are the twins you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes. And Vukasin Coveljic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall what time of day it was?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. Kerkez, they will go back and correct that. Thank you for that. We just wanted the name, and then we'll go back and get the spelling correct. Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you remember what time approximately on the 14th of July, 1995, you were at Branko Beara's house?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Around lunch time. I'd say 2 p.m.. 2, 2.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you remember, sir, if anyone else was present other than Branko Beara?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes. I arrived there. He lives in Kosovska Street. I was the first to get to his place, and I was greeted by his parents, his mother, Nada, and his father. I haven't seen them for a while -- I had not seen them for awhile. We talked about how things were, and then I went with Branko to his room. That's where we stayed for the rest of the time while I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, approximately how long did you stay at the Beara apartment?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: About an hour or two, an hour and a half, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Were there other people that were in the apartment at that time other than those that you've mentioned already?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes. When I was there, Branko was there together with his father. I greeted him, and Nada was there as well. I used to see her a bit more frequently. We talked a bit, and there were some other guests, older people that I didn't know. I just waved, said hello, and went with Branko to his room.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you know what, if any, occasion they may have been celebrating?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I didn't know then. Once I was with Branko in his room, I asked him, how come your father is here, and he said that he arrived because it was his birthday, and that's how he got the money too.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did he tell you how long his father had been there, or do you remember how long -- when he arrived?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: No, I really don't. He didn't tell me anything of the sort. He just told me that he was there and he was quite happy to be able to have acquired the money for the trip.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you saw Mr. Beara there, as well, on that day, did you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes. We shook hands, and perhaps we talked for a minute or two. I asked him how he was, and then I followed Branko. Branco's room was on the right-hand side of the door. We talked a bit with his parents, and then I followed him to his room.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I have to ask you this, Mr. Kerkez, because we've met a couple of times, but do you recall the times that you and I have met?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I do. I think it was in mid-May for the first time and then after that twice in the course of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And the two meetings in August were where?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: They were held at the Balkan Hotel in downtown Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you may not really remember, but do you remember what restaurant in the Hotel Balkan we were at?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I remember it's on the ground floor, but I don't remember its name.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, prior to May of 2008 or mid-May, as you say, 2008, did you have an opportunity to meet with Milan Stanic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes. Around mid-April. Milan Stanic gave me a phone call, we met in his office at Stari Merkator in new Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And share with us, if you will, how is it that Milan Stanic and you got together at his office, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: The phone rang. He introduced himself and explained why he was calling me. I thought it had to do with me, Branko, Vukasin, Boris, and Emil still hung out together at the time, and we would sit down for a drink. Branco's birthday was on the 12th of April as well. We met -- I don't know if it was for his birthday or for some other reason, and we discussed our past vacations, and I'm quite good at remembering details, and I could remember a lot of things for each of the summers and the things that happened. I presume that Branko had been in contact with Mr. Milan Stanic, and he may have asked him to talk to me about what I could remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And any other meetings or discussions with Milan Stanic or any members of our Defence team that you recall other than those that you've mentioned and the most recent one when you came here, obviously, to The Hague? Do you remember any other meetings that you may have had with us?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you this -- I'm going to ask you this, sir: Are you certain that it was July 14th, 1995, that you were at the Beara house when Branko told you it was Mr. Beara's birthday and that you left subsequent the next day to this trip in Petrovac? Are you sure about the year and the month?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes. I remember it for several reasons. One of those is because once we learned that Branko would go, I rang up the lady in Petrovac and I told her to secure the fifth bed as well. While we were at Branco's place, I like to go out frequently, and I suggested that we should go out. It was a Friday, and on Fridays and Saturdays we usually went out. We discussed it a bit, and then we decided not to go out but, rather, to try and save some money for the vacation. I remember it being a Friday and that the next day, Saturday evening, we left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic, did the witness not say his vacation was between 16th July and 1st of August?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Initially, I think he said -- and I'm -- from my notes, I'm going the 16th through the 31st.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page 46, line 19.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'll clarify the issue because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you stated that your vacation was from the 16th through the 31st of July, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes, it is. I didn't count the 15th because that's when we set off. The first day of vacation was the 16th. We arrived at the seaside on the 16th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'm going to show you a couple of pictures and before I do, how did we -- strike that. Do you remember meeting with me at the Hotel Balkan restaurant and I asking you to see if you have any pictures or anything that could help us further understand and appreciate the fact that the vacation that you are dealing with and this meeting that you -- or this encounter with Mr. Beara in July of 1995 occurred? Do you remember us discussing that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And then what did you tell me, sir? Do you remember what you told me?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I remember. I think I said I supposed I had pictures because I had pictures from most of my vacations, and I have a few of them with me here. I thought I had more, but some have gotten lost on the way, I guess, but this is what I have left.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And then I asked you to give me those pictures, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And then a couple days or a day or two later, we met again in the Balkan Hotel, and you gave me those five photographs, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: No. We agreed that I should bring them. On the first occasion, I didn't have them with me and I couldn't locate all of them, and I handed them over to you just now. I tried locating some other photographs with the twins on them, but I wasn't able to.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If we can just have you for the record, with the Court's permission and the usher's assistance, go through ever so briefly these pictures to determine whether or not these are the ones you gave me and what they depict. Mr. Kerkez, if I may as proceed as they are placing the photographs on the ELMO. Are these the five photographs that you gave me which reflect that you and Branko Beara and others were in Petrovac in 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes, the first photograph is at the Perazica Dol beach. From left to right, we see a guy we met there from Zajecar. In the middle standing in the blue swimming suit is Branko; next to him, Boris Cukic; down left, that's me; then Emil Cukic and Vukasin Coveljic, this -- the beach some 2 and a half kilometres away from Petrovac next to the As Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And we're going to mark these as evidence. I'm not sure if the Court really needs to us to go through every picture. They're very similar in nature, but I don't think it's necessary, but if the Court wishes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Completely up to you, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. Kerkez, I have no further questions for you. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, you asked for ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic. Thank you, madame.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Ditto.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Sarapa.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: No questions, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So it's Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning to you. Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to my friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And good morning, Mr. Kerkez. My name is Kweku Vanderpuye. On behalf of the Prosecution, I'm going to put some questions to you in relation to your testimony. If there's anything I ask you that's not clear to you, just let me know, and I'll do my best to try and rephrase it or restate it in a way that we can better understand one another. Now, Mr. Ostojic just showed you a few photographs. Well, actually, just one but I understand there are five photographs that you managed to find concerning this vacation. And with respect to those photographs, I notice that you are actually depicted in a couple. So with respect to those photographs, can you tell us who took them?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I don't know. Probably a passerby that we asked to take photographs of us at the Perazica Dol beach. Well, that's a lot of -- where a lot of people from Belgrade spend their vacation. We knew a lot of people there. We probably asked someone to take photographs of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do we have the five photographs, please. If you could place them on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, I don't really have a way of identifying these photographs since they're not marked, but this first photograph that's on the ELMO depicts six individuals, and you named them from left to right just a moment ago, right, and that's you depicted in the left bottom corner of that photograph, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Can we put another photograph on there, please. Thank you very much. All right. And can you tell us who the individuals in this photograph are?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: The same company as on the previous photograph. The left-hand side guy is the one that I don't know because we met him there, and then there's Emil, Vukasin, Branko, myself, and Boris. It's between Petrovac and Perazica Dol. The island is a landmark of Petrovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And that's you depicted second from the right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: The island is something you can see on every postcard.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And that's you the second from the right in that photograph, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: By the way, it's a landmark. What's the name of that island?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Excuse me?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: This island is a landmark, you said. What its name?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I don't know. I never did. It is characteristic, however, because it's some 500 metres away from Petrovac. We tried to swim out to the island on a couple of occasions, but we never managed to. There's a church there, I think, as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, you'd been there, you said, three summers in a row, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next one.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I was there a fourth summer, as well, some five years later with a girlfriend of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And you -- is it that you don't recall the name of the islands, or you never learned what its name was?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I think it bears the name of a saint, but I don't know. I never inquired. I merely liked looking at it from the beach. I can tell you the names of the bars there, but I can't tell you the name of the island.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Fair enough. Let's go to the next picture, please. All right. This one doesn't seem very clear on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you change the angle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The three fingers, it was Branko swimming in the sea holding the camera and taking a picture of us. That, I remember distinctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Branco's holding the camera and taking the picture; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: And swimming, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So those are his fingers there, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And we can go to the next one, please. All right. That's you in the middle, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And who are the two individuals on either side of you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Well, the left-hand side, Boris Cukic, and then Emil Cukic, the right-hand side. It's in front of the house where we spent the summer. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And where is the house that you spent the summer, by the way?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: In Petrovac, close to a restaurant which is a well known restaurant. It's called Voda U Krsu, some 20 metres away from the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is that all of them? Okay. What I've noticed about these photographs is that they're not -- they don't share the same dimensions. So what I wanted to ask you is, are these photographs that were developed from different films?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: No. It was one roll, but these pictures may have been developed -- or printed in different shops. I had a lousy camera at the time. Out of the 36 photographs, maybe 15 turned out in total. But it's the same roll of film; that, I'm sure of.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You printed the same roll of film in different shops? Is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes. These photographs are the ones I made. We may have exchanged each other's photographs, and they may have been printed in different shops. These are the ones I was able to find at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No, I understand that. My question is whether or not you developed these films or perhaps you were given these photographs from somebody else.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I developed them, but then the twins developed their own, and everyone else did. I can't tell you exactly which were printed by me.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Well, with respect to the ones that were printed by you, where did you have them developed?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I can't remember, but I remember that I went to the Lipa company because they were cheap. They were actually the cheapest in Belgrade, somewhere around the Boulevard of the Revolution in Belgrade, if I can remember it well. Currently, the street name is the Boulevard of King Aleksandar.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And do you remember when you had them developed?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Immediately after the end of that holiday.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So that would have been around when, exactly?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I suppose it was in August. I don't think that it was even more than ten days after. As soon as we returned I developed them, and I remember that I was really disappointed to see how many photos actually turned out well of the whole roll of film.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Now, in these photographs, you say this is in 1995, you would have been 17 years old; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Your friend Branko, how old was he at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: The same age. The difference between the two of us is two months. I was born on the 15th February, and he was born on the 12th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Boris?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: We were all of the same age. Boris's birthday is in October, 23rd of October. Actually, the twins were born on the 23rd of October, and Vukasin was born seven days after on the 20th. We were all peers. We went to the same grade. We are of the same age.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, you were asked a few questions about when it was that you were contacted by the members of the Defence for Mr. Beara. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I remember that Milan Stanic called me, introduced himself as a lawyer, and we met in mid-April this year in his office.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And where did he call you? Where were you when you received this call?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: You mean at the moment when the phone went off or where we met?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No, where the phone went off, where you received the call.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And did he introduce himself on the telephone when you spoke to him?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes, he introduced himself. He gave me his first and last names. He said that he was Branco's father's lawyer and that he would like to meet with me to talk about the summer 1995. I suppose that before that Branko had spoken to him and told him that I remembered that summer.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Do you remember the date that he called you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you remember the day of the week that he called you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: No. I remember the time that we met, but I don't remember when he called me. I know that it was sometime in mid-April that I went to his office, and I believe that he called me just a day before that, and I paid a visit to his office on the 15th of April, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did he explain to you on the telephone when he called you what he wanted to speak to you about in particular?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes, very briefly. It was a brief conversation, and I did not find this to be a problem. Branko is my friend. I was asked to talk about that summer. I went, did that without any prior explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, let's talk about when you went to meet Mr. Stanic for a little bit. Do you remember where you went to go meet him?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I remember. I went to his office, which is in the old Merkato building in new Belgrade on the second floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is that on a weekday or a weekend?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: It was on a weekday. It was raining. That's what I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Was it in the morning or the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Around noon. Around 11, 12, or maybe half past 12, but I know it was in the middle of the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you know where you came from to get to his office?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: From home. Actually, no, no, no, not from home. It was raining heavily, so I took my brother by car to Ada Ciganlija where he works as a diver. The traffic was very busy on that day. I had to cross a bridge. I was delayed in traffic, so I was late for the meeting, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And did you arrive at the meeting by yourself, or did you arrive there with anybody else?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: On my own. I parked the car, and I met up with Milan.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you met him in his office, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: He hadn't met you before, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So you introduced yourself, I take it; you sat down and you had a conversation with him, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You sat down; you had a conversation with him, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: He asked you questions about the summer of 1995, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, what did he ask you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Well, nothing much. He asked me what I remembered about that particular vacation, and I told him.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So he asked you in particular about the vacation; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: No. First we had a cup of coffee, and then I arrived at the conclusion that Branko and him had already had a conversation because maybe a week or so before that all of us had sat down and we reminisced on things such as parties and stuff, and then we also remembered that holiday that we were there all of us together, Vukasin -- the five of us. The summer before, that I spent my holiday with Vukasin Coveljic and in 1996 I holidayed with the twins and two other friends from my school, Miroslav and Dimitrij. So Branko realised that I remembered some of the details of summer of 1995, and I also remember that I organised a summer holidays in 1996 for some other friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: How many times have you met Mr. Stanic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Twice?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Because on page 61, line 14, of the transcript you refer to him as "Milan." Is that how you normally refer to him, by his first name?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: No, Mr. Milan Stanic. I never realized I was supposed to give his full name. I saw him then in his office and then at the Balkan hotel, and Mr. John -- Mr. John Ostojic, rather, was there as well. In Belgrade when I work that's how I call my superiors. I call them by their title, Mr. and then their first name, and that's a habit. So instead of referring to them by their full name, I only use their first names.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. So you gathered that Mr. Stanic had spoken to Branko Beara because you had a conversation with Branko Beara and the rest of your friends a week beforehand talking about this very vacation?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes, we discussed that summer as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What did you all recall together about that vacation when you sat down and talked about it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: We remembered some anecdotes, girls that we met and similar things, and we also remembered how it hadn't been very difficult for all of us to get together and spend the holiday together. It was a very specific situation because we had not known until the last moment whether Branko would go because there was no bed for him, and finally he ended up on a bunk bed. We had reserved four beds, and then he decided to join us. We did not change our reservations because we would have had to pay for that fifth bed, so we made it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I understand all that. What I'm asking you is what it is that you discussed when you sat down together and remembered this event together. You talked about the vacation, right, where you went?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I don't know. We talked about things that we had done. There were some girls that we liked. Then every day we went to this Perazica beach. It was interesting because we made our own meals; we tidied our room. For five of us together on the ground floor of that house, Branko, for example, liked to have a lie-in, so every morning I would throw grapes at him to wake him up. That was one of the anecdotes that we shared and remembered in that conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When was the last time you got together with your friends in that way before that conversation?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Before that conversation, we gathered for Branco's birthday. Branko took us out to the Plastic Disco Club on the 12th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So on the 12th of April, you went out for Branco's birthday; sometime after that, you had this conversation?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: It was possible even before that because we get together at least once a week. We get together in a pub, in my favourite pub where I always invite them to. Now, whether we had that conversation on a day before or after that evening -- well, whenever we go out we have a couple of drinks and we always talk about similar things.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. So the time you got together before you had this conversation, did you talk about these same things then as well?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: We always talk about the places we went to, the girls that we meet. I really can't remember the exact date when we mentioned that holiday, but we often talk about holidays. The next year I holidayed with the twins, but over the past five or six years we'll go spend holidays with our girlfriends, so our get-togethers during the summer have been somewhat reduced, and we miss that, so we like to go back to the days when we could spend holidays together.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No, I understand that, Mr. Kerkez, and I'm not asking you about habits and things that you usually do. I'm asking about a very specific thing, and what I'm asking you about this particular is, well, you say that you met Mr. Stanic and before that you had a conversation with Branko Beara concerning this vacation, and I'm asking you now about the time, any time, or the most recent time that you met with Branko Beara and your friends before that conversation. That's what I'm asking you. So I'd like to know if you can recall when was the last time you met Branko Beara before you had the conversation that was before you went to Mr. Stanic's office?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I understand what you are asking me. The last time I was with them, on the 12th of April in the evening in the Plastic Disco Club, but I can't remember when I spoke with Branko about that specific summer. I only concluded when Stanic had invited me for a conversation that Branko must have told him that I remembered the details of that holiday. But when it was that I actually talked about that with Branko, I really can't remember because there were several such conversations, so it's impossible for me to remember the exact date when I mentioned that particular holiday with Branko. And it was not just me who talked about that. There were the five of us, and it could have been even in March, and Branko could have remembered that and spoke to the lawyer and then the lawyer invited me to talk to him about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. So -- all right. You met Mr. Stanic. Mr. Stanic asked you certain questions. You say he asked you about that summer, right, summer of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what in particular did he ask you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Well, it was a relaxed conversation. He asked me what I remember. I really didn't know what was important, but I provided him with everything that I remembered about that particular summer.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, did he ask you in particular about July 1995 or June of 1995 or May or August of 1995? What specifically about the summer did he ask you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Well, nothing much. He asked me when I went on holiday and whether I remembered that, and I said I remembered exactly when I returned because it's the same every year. This year, for example, I spent my holiday with a girlfriend, and I remembered [as interpreted] on the 1st of August, and I remember this particular holiday because there were some problems with the five of us going, and I am very good with remembering people's birthdays, telephone numbers. I was the organiser of that particular holiday. I was in charge of arranging the accommodation. I knew that lady in Petrovac who was the landlady. I phoned her, and it took several conversations for me to confirm how many of us were finally coming.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sorry, I think I heard and we can always check it, on page 66, line 7, the witness said: "This year, for example, I spent my holiday with a girlfriend, and I returned on the 1st of August." But it says "I remembered on the first of August."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Ostojic. Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: At the time you were living with your parents, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The time that you met Mr. Stanic, you were living at home?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I live with my brother and my father. My mother died three years ago in 2005.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, at the time in 1995 that you discussed with Mr. Stanic, you were living at home, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes. I lived with my parents and my brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you told him that, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And he asked for their names, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes. Branislav and Ljubisa are my parents.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking you whether or not Mr. Stanic asked you those questions.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes, he did. I introduced myself and, yes, he did ask me.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: He asked you how to get ahold of them, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: He didn't ask to get ahold of the people you were living with back in 1995 when you took that vacation? He didn't ask you that question?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And you didn't give him that information either, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Information about what?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: How to reach your brother and whoever else you were living with in 1995 --

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: -- when you say you went on vacation?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: No, we did not talk about that. I only talked about the holiday and what I remembered of that holiday.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. When did you finish school that summer? When did you get out?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Around the 20th of June. That's the same every year.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please not overlap and make pauses between answers and questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Towards the -- mid-June all the marks are already in place, so nothing much goes on on the three or four last day of the school, and it's very difficult to remember the specific date when the school ends every year, but it's around the 20th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. But you don't remember now that I'm speaking to you, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: The last day of the school that year?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yeah. The last day of the school year in July -- in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: No, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: How long did this meeting last with Mr. Stanic in April when you met with him?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Not more than an hour. We exchanged words about that summer holiday. I told him what I remembered, and then I left.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And when you met with Mr. Stanic, he impressed upon you the importance of the information that you were giving him, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: No, not really. We just chatted. We just spoke about some details. It was only subsequently that I learned why I was supposed to come here.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When is it that you learned why you were supposed to come here?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: When I met up with Mr. John Ostojic on the second time round.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: During the time you spoke to Mr. Stanic in April, were you under the impression that you had to give him everything or tell him everything that you could remember about that summer?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: It was something like a spontaneous, relaxed chat. I did not feel hard-pressed to tell things. I just remembered things and told Mr. Stanic what I remembered about that summer.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. But were you -- let's say were you careful about what you said? Were you thinking about what you were telling him so as not to mislead him or give information incorrectly?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: No. I did not give it too much thought. I just told him how things were and what I remembered about that particular summer.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you tell him at the time that you met him in April that you had met with Branko Beara not a week before that and discussed the same thing with him? Did you tell Mr. Stanic that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you tell him that you discussed it amongst your other friends as well?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you ever tell Mr. Stanic that you had a discussion with Branko Beara about the subject matter of your testimony here today, which is this vacation in July of 1995? Did you ever tell Mr. Stanic about that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic invited me, introduced himself, and when I went to his office I assumed that he had already seen Branko, that Branko told him that I remembered that vacation, and that that was the reason why he had invited me to come for this meeting in his office. That's how I understood the whole situation. Otherwise, how would Mr. Stanic even knew that I existed had Branko not told him that we were friends and that we spent one summer together?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You make a very good point. Unfortunately, it doesn't answer my question. My question is, did you tell Mr. Stanic that you met with Branko Beara before you met with him? Did you tell him that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you ever tell him that? To this day that I'm talking to you now, did you ever tell him that you met with Branko Beara not a week before you met with him?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes. I told him just like I have told you that we get together quite often, at least once a week, and I never made it a point of telling him that I might have seen him two or three days prior to our meeting. At that time I did not find this important, just like I don't see any importance of that now. My conversation with Mr. Stanic was a relaxed, spontaneous exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. You met at a later point with Mr. Ostojic, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And when did that occur?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: In the second half of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Second half of May of this year, 2008, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: This year, yes. All of this has happened this year, my meeting with Mr. Stanic, my meeting with Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, let me put the same question to you, then, again: Did you ever tell Mr. Ostojic that you met with Branko Beara and discussed with him this vacation before you met with him, Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I did not tell him because I assumed that Mr. Ostojic knew that we had this habit of getting together and seeing each other every now and then.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, with all due respect --

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: It's only logical.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When you say you have this habit of getting together, what you are talking about is you have a habit of getting together and talking about a specific vacation in July 1995? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: No, that's not what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And so does it make any sense that Mr. Ostojic and Mr. Stanic have assumed that you've discussed these issues just because you get together?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I see where you are coming from, but what I'm saying is that I don't really know when it was when this subject of a vacation came up in one of our get-togethers, and I suppose that after that Branko spoke to Milan Stanic who then called me. I suppose that Branko said to Mr. Milan Stanic that he had seen me and that we had discussed things, summer holidays included, and that's why Stanic called me. And that's why I'm saying that I never saw the need to mention to anybody that the subject of summer 1995 came up in any particular conversation, and it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So but for your testimony here today - today - nobody knows how many times you've spoken to Branko Beara and the rest of your friends about the subject matter of your testimony, which is this vacation, because you didn't think to mention it to anybody; is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I apologise. I really don't understand; what are you asking me?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: How many times have you spoken to Branko Beara about this vacation that you have not told either Mr. Ostojic, Mr. Stanic, or anybody else?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think he mischaracterizes the testimony and the evidence that we've heard today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think so, but let me hear Mr. Vanderpuye. Can you explain where he is mischaracterising the testimony according to you, Mr. Ostojic, because frankly -- I mean, I'm not saying that you are not right but I can't see --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Maybe I'm having the same trouble as the witness understanding the question, so -- with all due respect. The way the question is put, there's two of them there, although the second one here says: "How many times have you spoken to Branko Beara about this vacation that you have not told either Mr. Ostojic, Mr. Stanic, or anyone else?" I'll object to the form of the question. I don't understand the question, either, but I think -- I think I know what he's trying to say, but I think it could be broken down so we can all understand it, if I can say that, with all due respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not really troubled with the question. If you follow up the previous questions and answers, particularly the one where he explained why he didn't bother to mention it. Yes. Mr. Vanderpuye, anyway, if you can be, perhaps, more clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'll try TO --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you could rephrase the question. I don't know. I'm not forcing you to because I think it's clear enough but --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I understand. If you are asking me how many times I may have spoken with Branko about that summer in the past 13 years, it could have been over 20 times.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Did you mention that to Mr. Stanic at any point before today?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: In that sense, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you mention that to Mr. Ostojic before today?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: That I had talked about it with my friends, reminiscing our summers?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No, no. Specific details about it, when it was taken, where you went, what you did, what bars you went to, what girls you saw, that kind of stuff.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ostojic knows that too. I told that to Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it's time for the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll have a 25-minute break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Kerkez.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I think when we left off I had just asked you about the information that you had provided to Mr. Ostojic and Mr. Stanic regarding your conversations with Branko Beara about this vacation. Now, when you met Mr. Stanic in April of this year, you told him about the vacation, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You told him where you went, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You told him how long you went for, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You told him that you went there by bus, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You told him that you left at night and you arrived in the morning in Petrovac, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you told him that you were at Branko's house the day before you left for your trip, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you tell him that you were there for about an hour or two hours, right, two or two and a half hours?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you told him in particular that you had met Mr. Beara and his wife, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You told him that there were other people that were there, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: People that you didn't know?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you told him that you left there without Branko, right, on that day?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: He stayed at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's right. You left his house and he stayed at home with his father and his mother and the other people in the house, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You told Mr. Stanic all of that in April of this year, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You told him that you were at that house on the 14th of July 1995, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, when you had this conversation with your friends before you met Mr. Stanic in April, you talked about the vacation that you had, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The vacation in 1995, in July 1995, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Sir, we don't -- I don't have an answer on the record, I don't think. If you could repeat your answer it would be, I think, helpful.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you talked about the bars that you went to and the girls that you saw, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you also talked about the fact that you were at Branko's house the day before you went on vacation, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you talked about the fact that you were at his house while his dad was there and his mom was there, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And that there was a party going on or there were other people in the house, right? You talked about that when you met with them before you met Mr. Stanic, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes, but it wasn't a party. There were some older people sitting there. Maybe they were around 50 -- their 50s or so. I just said hello and followed Branko to his room.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you talked about other vacations that you had together, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: You mean with my friends?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: With your friends.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what vacation did you talk about with them when you met with them before seeing Mr. Stanic other than the one in 1995? What vacation did you talk about with them?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I spoke with my friends about the summer of 1996, for instance, because all of us were there that year, save for Branko, and there were another two guys from the school. We were at the same house, and we had a good time that year as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So you went to the same place in Petrovac, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes. It was my third time to be in that house.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And when did you leave for that vacation?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: The same period, towards the end of August. But the next year we were there for about ten days because it became more expensive. Rather than a night being 10 German marks, it was 15, so we went later that year.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you remember what day, what date you went?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I can't recall the exact date, but I do remember being at the preparations in my club on the 1st of August; therefore, it must have been the end of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Right. Well, do you remember what you were doing the day before you left in 1996?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I don't. I did see the same guys I spent the summer with during the day, and we arranged who was going to take what, who was going to take food, ball, and we were at Dimitri's place in Sarajevska Street. He spent that summer with us, but I don't remember the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Let me just bounce back to 1995 for a minute, then. Do you remember what day you came back from Petrovac?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: It was a Saturday. It was exactly two weeks. I wanted to be back on Sunday to have a rest and start my practice on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Did you come back with all of your friends on that Saturday?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes. We had a return ticket from Belgrade, and we all headed back together.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. When you went down to Petrovac in the first place, you said you called a lady in advance to book a room or an apartment, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What was her name?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I don't remember. I did have her name and phone number jotted down in an address book, but it was then. I don't really remember it. I was back in 2003 with my girlfriend, but we didn't stay with that lady.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You don't remember her first name?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I don't. I only remember that the house was enormous and that one half the house belonged to one brother and the other half to the other brother, and the lady was one of the brothers' wife. I remember where the house was, but I can't recall her first or last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you know the address of the house?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: No. Visually, I know where it is, but I don't know what the address is. Petrovac is a small place. There may be three or four streets with a name there altogether.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, if I ask it this way, do you know the name of the street the house is on?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. When you went there in 1995, that wasn't the first time that you had been to that house; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: It was the second time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you've been there, you say, on how many occasions since?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: The next year, 1996, it was the third time. After that I didn't spend summers there. In the meantime I lost her phone number. Otherwise, I liked Petrovac as a place since the beach is towards the open sea, and when I was there in 2003 with my girlfriend, I couldn't find that lady's phone number, and we simply went to Petrovac and found accommodation there and then.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I see. So you were actually looking for that number in 2003; is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you believed you had it --

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Because I liked the house and the accommodation.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you believed you had that number even though the last time you had been there was in 1996?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes. I hoped so, because I tried to keep my notebooks and stuff, but I couldn't find that piece of information. When I was down in Petrovac, I did go to the very house, but they did not have any rooms available anymore, and we went to another house, which was further up the hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, during your meetings with Mr. Ostojic, of course, you let him know this, right, that is, that you couldn't remember the name of the lady whose house --

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You told him that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you told him where the house was as far as you could remember?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: No. I recalled now where it was. I told you that it was next to the restaurant Voda U Krsu, but as far as Mr. Stanic goes, I only told him it was in Petrovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. What about as far as Mr. Ostojic goes? Did you tell him it was next to this restaurant when you met him?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic? Who is that? No, I didn't share that detail with him, that the house was next to the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Didn't he ask you about where the house was?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: No, it's a small place.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I understand that, but I assume it has more than one house, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes, but I didn't share that detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And he didn't ask you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And he didn't ask you for the woman's name, either, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: He did, but I couldn't recall it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And when you met with Mr. Ostojic in May of 2008 at this Hotel Balkan, how long did you meet with him?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Not more than an hour, perhaps three-quarters of an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And when you met with Mr. Ostojic, he impressed upon you how important your testimony was, right, or the information, I should say, that you were giving him was, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes. But if I may add, there may have been another interesting thing. The reason why I remember that particular summer is this: Whenever we find -- we meet, we called Branko's father Pape between -- inside our circle, and we called him that because he spent a lot of time in Dalmatia and it's a common nickname there. Therefore, we always refer to him as Pape, and so we did on that occasion as well. And Vukasin keeps going back to that detail and telling us about in.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Vukasin keeps going back to that detail and telling you about it when? When did he tell you about it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Whenever we tried to recall that summer since, as I said already, that we didn't know if Branko was going to go. His father brought the money, and instead of bringing fresh food Branko had tin cans from the army, and he kept offering us that. We kept refusing. He had a military sack, and quite often Vukasin would tease him, oh, it was Pape who brought you the money.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, since you met Mr. Stanic in April, have you spoken to Branko or Vukasin or Boris or Emil?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: About that?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: About that.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes. But it was casual conversation, and I told them that I met with an attorney. We are really good friends, and we share all sorts of things, and I did mention I had that conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did Branko ever tell you that he met with an attorney?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: He didn't, but since it is his father who is here, I presumed he had contacts with attorneys. Otherwise, Branko didn't like discussing his father much.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And how many times did you converse with your friends about this subject after you met Mr. Stanic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Only once. Perhaps right after I saw Mr. Stanic. We don't talk about such things. We talk about other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You don't talk about things like what, like meeting lawyers?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we mention things. We share what is going on at our jobs or with our girlfriends, but after that we were talking about other new things.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And when you met with your friends and talked -- and told them that you had met with an attorney, what specifically did you tell them that you spoke about with the attorney?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Nothing. I just told him I saw this attorney, he is Branko's father's attorney, and I told him about the summer we spent together.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Any of your friends asked you about this attorney, what did he want to know, was it interesting, was it boring? They didn't ask you anything about it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: In principle, no. I told them about it. I told them Attorney-At-Law Milan Stanic called me because I presumed he had talked to Branko, and Branko in our conversation following the event when we met in early April probably talked to the attorney, and he told him that I recall things. When we were going back to that summer, I seemed to be the one who remembered the most out of the five.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Out of the five including Branko, are you saying?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You remember more than Branko does about this vacation and where you were before you left and everything?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Most likely.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, you say you seem to be the one that remembers the most. Why do you say that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Since he mentioned to Milan Stanic that I can recall many details, I presume that his recollection is poorer than mine. That's why I said probably or likely.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, you've talked to him about this vacation, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: With Branko?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: As I said, from time to time we go back to that vacation, but after I spoke with the attorney, we didn't discuss that particularly. For some reason of his, he noticed that I can recall many details. He probably gave my phone number to the attorney, and in turn he called me.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Having discussed this with him, what kind of details do you remember that he doesn't?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: For example, the date when we left, for example. He couldn't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: He doesn't remember the date that you left?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: He doesn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: He doesn't remember that the date that you left according to you was the day after his father's birthday, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Well, he remembers that, but he doesn't remember some details to the extent I do. For example, he doesn't remember the moment when we were sitting in a pizzeria and after a beer he sort of started staring into the distance and started crying because he said it reminded him so much of Split. He doesn't remember the name of the girl he liked at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. So Branko, Mr. Beara's son who stayed home on the 14th with his father, doesn't remember that he left that summer the next day, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: No, he remembers that for sure because his father brought him the money the day before the travel. He really wanted to go with us. Ever since he had left Split he had not seen the sea. I don't think he would forget that, but he forgot some other details which happened during the vacation itself. Your first question was whether my recollection of the vacation is better than Branko's, and I said most likely having in mind these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, what you said is: "For example, he doesn't recall the date when we left." That would be the 15th of July according to what you've testified to today, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Well, it was at the moment when I told you that he, as I said, probably doesn't remember the vacation better than I do, but each one of us friends remembers things. For example, I know that it was on the 14th in the evening. We liked going out on Friday, but I couldn't press them into it because Branko said he still didn't have the money, et cetera, et cetera. I remember all that, and he shared it with me when I joined him in his room. The rest of the guys joined with him because they didn't want him to be left out. I was the one who organised that vacation. I booked the room, and we had to go back for our sports preparations. That's how I recall the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Kerkez, isn't one of the reasons that you recall the date because Branko didn't go out with you because he said that it was his father's birthday? Isn't that one of the reasons why you recall the date?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: No, that's not the only reason. I remember it being a Friday. I remember we spent a fortnight at the sea. One of the things I remember was that Branko didn't want to go out with us because he had not seen his father for quite a long time and he wanted to stay with him, and they had guests.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I didn't ask you if it was the only reason. I asked you if it was one of the reasons. Did Branko tell you on the day that you went to his house that it was his father's birthday? Did he tell you that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And so your testimony is that he couldn't recall the date when you left, which was the next day, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: That's not right. Some five minutes ago, I told you that I remember more things about the vacation than Branko does.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's right, and I asked you for an example, right? And you said: "For example" --

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: -- "the date when we left." He couldn't recall that, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: That is right. I did say that, but then I corrected myself because all five of us frequently remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When you met with Mr. Ostojic in May of 2008, you met with him for about an hour, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did he take notes about what you were telling him?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes. He was writing it down.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And he wrote down what you told him, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: He wrote down some things with a pencil on a plain sheet of paper. He would jot down a word or two.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And what about when you met Mr. Stanic in April 2008? Did he write down what you were saying?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: No, he did not keep any notes as far as I recall. We only talked.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And you met with Mr. Ostojic just recently, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Right. In August.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In August. And what did you discuss with him when you met with him the second time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Specifically, he told me that I will have to come here to testify about the summer.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And in particular about the 14th of July, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Your recollections of being in the Beara house on the 14th of July, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you tell him at that time that you had a conversation with Branko about these particular circumstances?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. Whether I talked to him on that day, the 14th of July, or --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'll rephrase the question. Did you tell Mr. Ostojic in August or in May that you had had a conversation with Branko Beara after you met with Mr. Stanic about these circumstances? Did you tell Mr. Ostojic that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Not directly, but Mr. Ostojic must have presumed that we talked about it since we hang out together frequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When you say "not directly," does that mean, no, you didn't tell him that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I didn't tell him that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you tell Mr. Ostojic that Branko could not recall the events that you could recall?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I did not because, to repeat, my presumption is that Mr. Milan Stanic got in touch with me because Branko estimated that I could recall the most details of the five. That's probably the same reason why I later met Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Was that what Mr. Stanic told you? Did he tell you that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: What? That Branko had given him my phone number or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No, that Branko estimated that you could recall the most details of the five of you? Did he tell you that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: No, he didn't tell me that. That is my assumption, and I usually remember more than anybody else when it comes to certain things.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, do you remember more than the other friends that you have in common, like Boris and Emil? Do you remember more than them about this summer of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
