utterances.text: All right. Well, what kinds of things do you remember that they don't about this trip?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you why. I was the main organiser of the whole trip, and they just end up and had a good time. I bought their bus tickets and reserved the room, and they just met me at the departure points, so I suppose that some of those things they can't remember because they were not important. They just are not in the position to remember, and as for what happened while we were there on the coast, I suppose that all of us remember more or less the same things. I was very heavily involved in the organisation, much more than any of them, and that's why I remember those things particularly well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did they ever tell you that they couldn't remember the date that you left?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: As I say, we did not talk much after my conversation with Mr. Stanic. I told them that I met up with the lawyer, but we did not talk much. I never spoke with them about the possibly -- the possibility of them remembering the date. I consider that an opportunity to ask them. It didn't come up.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. But it came up before you met Mr. Stanic, and it just so happened that during the course of this conversation, a week before you met Mr. Stanic, that you discussed this vacation in 1995 and that you stopped at Branko's house and met Branko's mother and father. That just happened to come up; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: No, I didn't mention it then. I just assumed that Branko estimated that I had remembered more than anybody, and when Mr. Stanic asked me, I gave him all the details, not in the way I normally talk to my friends because when I talk to my friends it's not a question-and-answer session. It's a spontaneous, relaxed conversation. When you get together to your friends, are you quizzed or do you expect to have to answer questions from them? I suppose that you talk spontaneously in a relaxed manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, indeed I do. I'm glad you asked. But how is it that when you get together with your friends and talk about and reminisce about the past, you just happen to come up with a conversation that concerns the subject matter of your testimony and a meeting that comes up a week later?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I really did not select the moment when we will talk about that. It so happens we have a beer, we get involved in a conversation about the times past. I don't know when Branko had got in touch with Milan Stanic. I only know that Milan Stanic asked me to come to his office to talk about that particular summer, and during that conversation I shared with him some details of that summer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How much more do you have?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Not that much more, Your Honour. I think about -- well, we're done in 10 minutes, right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, I think it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think I can finish in 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there re-examination? Not that you know of.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Not likely, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When Branko called you to come over to his house in July - this is just before you left - where were you when you got this call?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: At home. There were no mobile phones at the time. I was home, and the distance between our two houses is maybe ten minutes. He asked me to come over, and I walked to his place, and then when I got there he told me that he would be joining us on that holiday.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did he invite anybody else over, any of Your other friends?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Boris, Emil, and Vukasin were also there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So those two were also at the house at the same time as you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Actually, three.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. They were all at the house at the same time as you, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: They all met Mr. Beara, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I suppose so. Well, I was the first one to arrive there, and we waited for the others to turn up. They live a bit further away. I don't know whether they spoke to the parents or whether Branko opened the door and took them immediately to his room.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Well, they were in the house at the same time as Mr. Beara, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Which Mr. Beara? They were both there. We were all there at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Just joking. Yes, we were all in the house. We were in Branko's room, the five of them, and then in the living-room and on the terrace. Mr. and Mrs. Beara were entertaining their guests.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And when you met Mr. Beara, what was he wearing?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I really can't remember. I believe that he had short sleeves and short trousers. It was summer, after all, but I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And what were they doing when you arrived at the apartment?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Branko answered the door, and maybe two steps behind I saw his father standing. I suppose he was also expecting somebody. I greeted Branko's father. I had not seen him in a long time. We exchanged pleasantries. He was always in a good mood. He was always joking. He was laughing at something. I spent maybe a couple of minutes in casual conversation with him, and then Branko took me to his room.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, when was the time that you saw him before that time? When was the time you last saw him?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I really can't remember. I did see him every now and then when he was in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. So you don't remember the time you saw him before that day, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I hadn't seen him in a long time, so when I saw him that time around, I was taken by surprise. I asked him how he was doing. I suppose I had not seen him for maybe two or three months, even.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Well, truth be told, I wasn't in their house every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, you've been to that house, I assume, on a number of occasions, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes, quite often.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You know the house very well, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Had anything in the house changed since the last time you were there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Has anything changed since the last time or had something changed? Well, things have changed over the 10 or 15 years that they've lived there but not much. There is, however, major change. They laid laminate floor in the apartment since they first moved in, but that's about all.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Perhaps my question was a little inartful. Had anything in the house changed before the time you were last there and the time that you were there and you saw Mr. Beara and his wife and the guests, et cetera? Had anything changed, furniture or things like that? Anything change?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: No, no. They have old furniture. I believe that they had moved it from Split when they arrived in Belgrade, and they still have that same furniture. The rooms are the same; the walls are the same. Nothing has changed since they first moved in.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. When you got back from your vacation you went to your training, you said, right? This is handball training.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: We arrived at the weekend. I took a day to rest. My then-coach Pera Lazarevic, an Olympian, had the same system. He started preparations on the 1st of September. Since the 1st of September was a weekend, we started on Monday. There was a competition to be held soon, and we started our preparations on the first Monday after the 1st of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Did you tell Mr. Ostojic and Mr. Stanic that your coach's name was Pera Lazarevic? Did you tell them that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you told him that you started on the 1st of September, your training? You told them that too?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: The 1st of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The 1st of August?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And they wrote that down?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: I don't know. I suppose they did. I was not watching them take notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just -- again, I think we were having just a little trouble with the transcript and what he's saying and what the translation is, but we'll look at the tape again and then come back to it at this point, just so the Court knows.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And among your friends, are you the only one that's involved in this training?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: No, Branko, Bare [phoen], and myself, we were in training together. I started practicing handball in 1992, and later on in the first grade of high school Branko asked me whether I could talk to my coach to take him on. So in 1993 he started, but his handball career was short-lived because in 1996 he was injured in a game. He had to undergo a surgical procedure, and that's when he stopped training.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So he went back to training with you in 1995, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Yes. We were still junior players at the time, and we were supposed to join the senior team, and that's why we had to work much harder than anybody else, and we had to be there on Day 1 every season.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And he recalls that, you having spoken to him about it, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: About training?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yeah, about when training started in 1995, in the summer of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KERKEZ
utterances.text: Oh, he know it. Of course, he does. That was the common practice in the team. Every year the championship ended in mid-June, then there was a break, we had to come back in the beginning of August, and then the season started.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I have no further questions at this time, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. No re-examination, Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Questions? Are you related to Zeljko Kerkez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Doesn't ring a bell. I'm often asked in Belgrade about some doctors who share my family name, and they ask me if I'm related to them, and my answer is always no. I don't know these people, and I don't know the person that you asked me about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. That brings an end to your testimony. You are free to go. You will receive assistance from our staff. On behalf of the Trial Chamber, I wish to thank you for having come over, and I also wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we have a very brief housekeeping matter that Mr. Thayer will address on scheduling?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. We can do the documents next Monday. That's the photos -- there are the photos, and practically that's it. You don't have any other things apart from the photos, do you?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I do not, Mr. President. 2DIC 213 would be the only document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. Those are going to be -- no objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No, there's no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have to be really quick because I'm advised we can't stay a minute longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I understand there's another matter following us, Mr. President. We are in receipt of the witness schedule for next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just given the -- some recent history, I just wanted to -- for everybody's sake to find out what the actual schedule is going to be. We had Mr. Subotic on the schedule, and Wagenaar at one point was scheduled for prior to some of these other witnesses. So I wanted to just find out if we can clarify if it's going to be Subotic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can find out with Mr. Ostojic and then let us know, if Mr. Ostojic knows. I suppose you do.
